claim: When an MCP server declares readOnlyHint on a tool, pin the claim to behaviour with a stub-transport probe that drives every read-only handler against a recording client and refuses any POST to a route not allow-listed with a reason (and static-check that route's source for write primitives), because a host may relax consent on the hint and a write wearing read-only is the failure that auto-approves.
because: pof-mcp shipped 49 annotations this way; fault-injecting one write tool to read-only failed the guard on its exact POST, and reading the routes found one description-identical write (saveRun) among eight pure POSTs.

claim: When a stdio tool server cannot rely on tools/listChanged, ship progressive discovery as an OPT-IN static group gate plus an always-visible discovery tool, not a trimmed default, because an unattended agent cannot re-list its way back to a capability the host hid.
because: Gating 49 tools on pof-mcp: the sprawl standard says load what the task plausibly needs, but its worked examples assume an attended host that can activate a group mid-session. MCP clients honour listChanged unevenly, so a core-only default would have silently removed capability from an autonomous harness run with no recovery path. Landed the inverse - all groups on unless POF_MCP_TOOL_GROUPS trims them, a pof_tool_groups meta-tool that is never gated and lists every hidden group WITH its tool names, and refusal-at-the-door naming the group so listed-is-callable holds in both directions.

claim: When a module owns a corrupt-vs-missing distinction for a persisted file, grep every other reader of that file name for a raw parse-with-fallback, because an API edge that JSON.parses the same file and returns the fallback on catch silently re-collapses corrupt into empty.
because: pof harness: state-io.ts made game-plan/progress corruption fatal in the loop; GET /api/harness?action=progress read progress.json by hand and mapped a truncated file to [] (fixed a53c933f, test reproduces the truncated write).

claim: When a loop repairs a failure and then re-runs the failing check to confirm the repair, the confirmation must run under the SAME limits as the gate that produced the failure - same output budget, same timeout, same judging rule - because a confirmation that is stricter than its gate converts a successful repair into a fresh failure and spends the next retry on a measurement artefact.
because: attemptSelfHeal re-ran the failing gate's own command through exec with Node's 1MB default maxBuffer while the verifier runs that identical command at 10MB; exec kills the child and returns ENOBUFS on overflow, so a chatty-but-passing tsc/UBT re-run reported 'verify command still failing after the fix session'. Fixed and seeded: only the loud-success case goes red when the budget is reverted.

claim: When a test asserts that a rule now holds UNIFORMLY across a closed set of kinds, derive the case population from the type that defines the set (a Record over the union, which fails to compile when a member is added) rather than from a hand-written list - because the member the author forgot to list is the member where the rule is still broken, and the hand-written list makes that absence read as coverage.
because: gate-honesty.test.ts opened 'no gate self-certifies ... it is now uniform' and enumerated 6 of the 10 members of VerificationGate['type']; the visual branch - one of the 4 omitted - still answered passed:true when it had nowhere to write captures, and had done so through every prior green run of that file. Replacing the list with Record<VerificationGate['type'], ...> put the broken member inside the population and it failed immediately.

claim: When a UI offers a re-run as a fix, derive whether the re-run CAN change anything from the producer's own code (an arity probe of the produce body, with an explicit override where arity lies) rather than from a declared flag, because a flag on hundreds of specs is a claim about the body that rots out of step with it.
because: PoF wave 26 (cb0b2f09): 344 of 344 registered produce bodies ignored the direction, so the headline Produce fix was a byte-identical no-op on ~303 steps; the arity probe + shrink-only linter ratchet withheld the button honestly and needed no per-spec authoring.

claim: A producer stamp on an artifact must be written by the party that can PROVE the producer ran: let a client declare only engines it can assert about itself (deterministic code), refuse remote-engine claims with a 400, and preserve a claimed engine only when the server already recorded that same engine on that exact row, because a client-writable stamp is the fabricated-pass hole reopened one field over.
because: PoF wave 26 (7c7b7872): 817/817 artifacts had no recorded engine; the one-shot route now stamps Claude{model,effort} from the same object it hands to the dispatcher, the artifacts route refuses top-level Claude via a zod enum and downgrades a smuggled data._provenance claim to unknown unless the row already attests it (the lab write-through re-POSTs what the server persisted).

claim: Before authoring a provenance label across hundreds of items, measure how often the existing heuristic DECIDES the displayed value and how often it agrees with an audit where both exist; if the heuristic decides almost nothing, the campaign is unwarranted and the honest fix is to author only where the code reads unambiguously and document the agreement rate.
because: PoF wave 27 (9bdc466d): the /status engine heuristic decided 6 of 344 cells and named none of them (27% agreement where it would have named one over an audit), so a planned 300-step authoring pass was closed by measurement; 129->189 authored where the code was legible.

claim: When two engines must agree on a generated layout, ship the layout as DATA one engine exports and the other replays, and state the parity rung in the agreement reason itself (exact by construction on the data; runtime placement unverified until observed) rather than promising seed-reproducibility across regenerating engines.
because: PoF wave 28 (d09208ac): the browser preview and the UE generator could never agree from a seed (LLM regenerates freehand); a grid-replay engine consuming the exported cells made one pair exact by construction while the reason string carries UNVERIFIED for runtime placement.

claim: The empty-state taxonomy types emptiness by three causes (nothing exists yet / nothing matches the query / nothing visible at this permission level) and misses a fourth that fires on every schema-driven body: data ARRIVED and this view cannot render its shape. Rendering the nothing-yet empty state there is the same class of lie the technique already forbids for failure, because it reports a step that ran as a step that never ran. The rule to add: when the body is rendered from a caller-supplied view descriptor over free-form data, an unrenderable-but-present payload gets its own state that names expected vs actual, and only a genuinely absent payload may claim emptiness.
because: pof at 01816c1e: ViewPanel splits resolveTableView into absent / mismatch / rows-or-values and renders a dedicated ShapeMismatch that names expected vs actual (src/components/layout-lab/steps/ArchetypeStep.tsx:59, dispatched at :85-87) rather than the absent branch's shared empty text at :84. Its own comment at :78-82 records the measured cost of the collapsed version: assuming the columns live at the top level 'rendered 28 tables as nothing but -- missing', i.e. 28 produced artifacts read as unproduced.
